doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Wartime Cotton Club band in Cincinnati, day jobs and family
summary: During the war he played dances and floor shows at the Cotton Club in Cincinnati, worked at Curtiss Wright and shined shoes in high school; his father was a laborer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you have experience — what would World War II bring for you?
World War II? Well during the war I was in a band in Cincinnati, Ohio, at the Cotton Club. And we played there, we played maybe three or four sessions a day.
Yeah. Dancing and the floor show.
And then you started — did you ever have to work non musical jobs to get by?
Oh yeah. During the war I worked at Curtiss Wright, and made airplane engines, and swept the floor, mopped the floor.
Played at night? Played gigs at night?
Yeah. When I was in high school I used to shine shoes. My father got me a job at a couple of barber shops shining shoes.
What did your father do for a living?
Five. My brother and sister and my mother and father.
